title: Rainfall Accumulation and Dry-Spell Tracker
dataSources: Weather-station observations (`ecowitt:obs`, `weatherflow:obs`), air-quality readings (`purpleair:aqi`, `airgradient:sensor`), soil/greenhouse sensors, aquarium controllers.
app: Personal weather stations (Ecowitt/Ambient/Davis/WeatherFlow), air-quality sensors (PurpleAir/AirGradient), and aquarium/greenhouse/soil sensors via HEC and MQTT.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=ecowitt:obs
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(rain_mm) as rain_mm by _time
| streamstats current=t sum(eval(if(rain_mm=0,1,0))) as dry_streak reset_after="(rain_mm>0)"
| sort - _time
description: Tracks daily rainfall and counts consecutive dry days so gardeners know exactly when to water and when nature has done it for them.
value: A running dry-spell counter saves both water and plants by turning 'has it rained lately?' into a definite number.
implementation: Ingest weather-station rainfall; schedule daily and use the dry-streak counter to guide watering.
visualization: Column chart of daily rainfall with a dry-streak overlay.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks how much rain fell and how many dry days in a row, so you know exactly when the garden needs watering.
